title: Context-Aware Content Safety Review Pattern
description: A pattern for testing a generative content feature's output against context-specific prompt categories — including cases where a global safety or fairness adjustment could conflict with factual accuracy — before staged public release.
problem: A safety or fairness adjustment tuned and tested against one broad category of prompts (e.g. generic requests for people) can produce absurd or harmful results on a different category (e.g. historically specific requests) if that category was never tested separately, and the failure often surfaces only after public release.
solution: Enumerate the distinct prompt categories a generative feature will plausibly be used for, including ones where a safety/fairness adjustment could conflict with factual or historical accuracy, and test each category explicitly before release; release first to a limited audience with a fast feedback channel and a rollback path, expanding to full availability only after the limited release surfaces no material issues.
applicability: Any generative content feature (image, text, audio, or video) being released or materially updated for public or broad internal use.
consequences: Enumerating every plausible prompt category is inherently incomplete; staged rollout delays full availability and requires monitoring infrastructure to detect issues during the limited-release phase.

citations.title: Gemini image generation got it wrong. We'll do better.

relationships.reason: Context-specific testing before release is the concrete mechanism satisfying this control.
The pattern's output is a content safety review report.
